children: Indonesian shares slipped 34 points or 0.5% to 6,652 in Wednesday morning trade, reversing the prior rally as tech, non-cyclicals, and finance weighed on sentiment.
Traders stayed cautious ahead of August consumer confidence data later today, after July’s reading hit a 15-month low.
Meanwhile, July retail sales will be due Thursday, after June's reading marked three straight month of declines.
Globally, U.S. futures were mixed after Wall Street’s overnight losses, pressured by oil near $100, inflation fears, and bond yields at multi-year highs.
In main trading partner China, August CPI accelerated as expected, with PPI topping forecasts, adding to regional inflation concerns.
Still, losses were limited by Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa’s assurance that Indonesia's GDP growth would remain solid in Q3 and Q4 despite recent natural disasters.
Notable laggards included Charoen Pokphand (-3.0%), Bumi Resources (-1.9%), Indo Tambangraya Megah (-1.7%), and Astra International (-1.6%).

title: Indonesian Equities Retreat After Tuesday Rally
